title: Not by reasoning
theme: This understanding is not reached by reasoning but by being taught by another; Death praises Naciketas’ true resolve and wishes for questioners like him.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «स्वबुद्ध्यभ्यूहमात्रेण», by one’s own conjecture alone

words.meaning: to be attained; (or) to be taken away

words.role: object of आपः; refers to मतिः

sandhi.rule: matiḥ (from mati + s, P. 8.2.66 (ससजुषो रुँः)) keeps its r before a vowel.
proktā + anyena: ā + a give ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः). anyena + eva: a + e give ai, P. 6.1.88 (वृद्धिरेचि).

sandhi.type: final m before a consonant and before a vowel
sandhi.rule: yām before t: P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः). tvam keeps its m before ā.
satyadhṛtiḥ before b shows r. bata + asi: P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).

sandhi.type: stop before a nasal; aḥ before a voiced consonant
sandhi.rule: tvādṛk before n becomes the nasal ṅ, P. 8.4.45 (यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा). naḥ before bh: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च), P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः). bhūyāt before n becomes bhūyān, by the same P. 8.4.45 (यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा).

samasa.meaning: one whose resolve is true; Śaṅkara: «सत्या अवितथविषया धृतिर्यस्य तव स त्वं सत्यधृतिः»

morphology.note: A gerundive in -eya whose root Śaṅkara leaves open. He glosses it first as ‘to be attained’, «नापनीया न प्रापणीयेत्यर्थः», and then as ‘to be removed, destroyed’, «नापनेतव्या वा ; नोपहन्तव्या», which takes it from apa-nī ‘lead away’. Raṅgarāmānuja has only the first: «तर्केण प्रापणीया न इत्यर्थः».
Aorist second singular of āp ‘obtain’: a root marked with ḷ takes the thematic aorist, P. 3.1.55 (पुषादिद्युताद्यॢदितः परस्मैपदेषु); a + āp gives āp-: āpaḥ, ‘you have obtained’.

tvādṛś ‘like you’: dṛś after a pronoun, P. 3.2.60 (त्यदादिषु दृशोऽनालोचने कञ् च), with the pronoun’s final ā, P. 6.3.91 (आ सर्वनाम्नः); the final consonant becomes k, P. 8.2.62 (क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः).
Precative (a wish) of bhū, P. 3.4.116 (लिङाशिषि): ‘may there be’.
praṣṭṛ ‘one who asks’, an agent noun of prach ‘ask’, P. 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ). GRETIL’s प्रेष्टा is a copying error that repeats preṣṭha of the line before (corrections.json).
Superlative of priya ‘dear’, with priya replaced by pra- (the same rule as preyas in 1.2.1): ‘dearest’.

translation.literal: ‘This understanding is not to be attained by reasoning; taught by another, dearest, it is for good knowing. You have obtained it; ah, you are one whose resolve is true. May there be for us, Naciketas, a questioner like you.’
translation.readable: ‘This understanding cannot be reached by argument. It is when another teaches it, my dear, that it is truly understood. You have found it — and how steadfast you are! May we always have a questioner like you, Naciketas.’

anvaya: प्रेष्ठ, एषा मतिः तर्केण न आपनेया; अन्येन एव प्रोक्ता [सती] सुज्ञानाय [भवति] । याम् त्वम् आपः, [त्वम्] बत सत्यधृतिः असि । नचिकेतः, त्वादृक् प्रष्टा नः भूयात् ।
syntax: Two statements about the understanding, one negative (not by reasoning) and one positive (taught by another, it serves good knowing), with a vocative between them; a relative clause (yāṃ tvam āpaḥ) links them to Naciketas, followed by an exclamation of praise (satyadhṛtir batāsi) and a wish in the precative (tvādṛṅ no bhūyāt … praṣṭā).

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: another than the logician, a teacher who knows scripture, «अन्येनैव आगमाभिज्ञेनाचार्येणैव तार्किकात्». Raṅgarāmānuja: a teacher other than oneself, «स्वस्मादन्येनैव गुरुणा». Madhva cites this line to show that in 1.2.8 the ‘non-other’ who cannot teach is the one who does not see the Lord as other: «प्रोक्ताऽन्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ इति वाक्यशेषात्».

ambiguities.topic: āpaneyā: ‘to be attained’ or ‘to be removed’
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara gives both: the understanding cannot be reached by reasoning, and it cannot be taken away or destroyed by it, «नापनेतव्या वा ; नोपहन्तव्या». The second sense makes the verse a defence of scriptural knowledge against the logician, whom Śaṅkara describes as one who imagines whatever his own mind constructs: «तार्किको ह्यनागमज्ञः स्वबुद्धिपरिकल्पितं यत्किञ्चिदेव कल्पयति».

ambiguities.topic: ‘May there be for us a questioner like you’
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: another son or pupil, «भवत्वन्यः पुत्रः शिष्यो वा प्रष्टा»; Death says it in compassion, to praise the knowledge he is about to give, «अनुकम्पयन्नाह मृत्युर्नचिकेतसं वक्ष्यमाणविज्ञानस्तुतये». Raṅgarāmānuja: «त्वादृशः शिष्यः अस्माकं भूयादित्यर्थः».

beginner: Death finishes his praise of the boy before beginning the teaching itself. The understanding Naciketas is seeking cannot be reached by argument alone; it becomes clear when someone who knows it teaches it. Naciketas has already taken hold of it, in the sense that he has fixed his mind on it and refused every distraction. Death calls him “dearest” and says, with real warmth, that his resolve is true. Then he says something surprising for the god of death: he wishes he always had pupils like this one. Teachers know the feeling. A good question is a gift to the person who is asked it, and the rare student who keeps asking it, steadily, is what makes teaching worthwhile.
analogy: Like an old teacher who, after years of indifferent pupils, meets one who will not stop asking the real question, and says, ‘I wish all my students were like you.’

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: That this understanding is not to be had by reasoning but is well understood when taught by another; that Naciketas has obtained it and is steadfast; and that Death wishes for questioners like him.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: the understanding that arises from scripture, «येयमागमप्रभवा मतिः», cannot be reached by one’s own conjecture alone, «स्वबुद्ध्यभ्यूहमात्रेण»; it is understood when taught by a teacher who knows scripture. In his Brahmasūtra-bhāṣya (2.1.6) he quotes this line to show that Brahman is known from scripture alone, like dharma: «आगममात्रसमधिगम्य एव त्वयमर्थो धर्मवत्».

commentary.q: In what sense has Naciketas ‘obtained’ it already?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: through the boon Death granted, «मद्वरप्रदानेन». Raṅgarāmānuja: he has resolved to attain it, «सिषाधयिषिततया निश्चितवानित्यर्थः»; his resolve cannot be shaken, «सत्या - अप्रकंप्या धृतिः यस्य स तथोक्तः».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: For Śaṅkara, a teacher learned in scripture as opposed to the logician; for Raṅgarāmānuja, a teacher other than oneself; for Madhva, commenting at 1.2.8, the one who knows the Lord as other than the self, the ‘other’ who completes the sense of ananya there: «प्रोक्ताऽन्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ इति वाक्यशेषात्».

advaita.text: The knowledge of the self comes from scripture through a teacher, and reasoning alone can neither reach it nor overturn it: «अत एव च येयमागमप्रभूता मतिः अन्येनैव आगमाभिज्ञेनाचार्येणैव तार्किकात्, प्रोक्ता सती सुज्ञानाय भवति».

visistadvaita.text: Even one skilled in reasoning cannot know it by himself; taught by a teacher other than oneself it becomes the means of release: «उपदिष्टैव मति: - मोक्षसाधनाय भवति».

dvaita.text: Madhva uses this line as the completion of 1.2.8: the knowledge comes only from ‘another’, one who knows the Lord as other than the self, «प्रोक्ताऽन्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ इति वाक्यशेषात्». His comment filed with 1.2.9–10 concerns 1.2.10.

schools.disagreement: All three make a teacher necessary. They differ on who he is: one who knows scripture rather than the logician (Śaṅkara), a realised teacher other than oneself (Raṅgarāmānuja), or one who knows the difference of the Lord and the self (Madhva).

parallels.quote: नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ
parallels.note: Śaṅkara quotes the line in the Brahmasūtra-bhāṣya, with the reference (क. उ. १ । २ । ९), to show that Brahman is known from scripture alone.
‘Because reasoning has no firm ground …’: the Brahmasūtra’s own statement that reasoning cannot settle what scripture teaches.

contemporary.text: Some understanding is passed on rather than worked out: a craft, a language, a way of seeing. A student who insists on deriving everything alone can become very clever and still miss it. The verse is not against thinking — Naciketas thinks hard — but it says that this kind of understanding arrives through a relationship. And it ends with the teacher’s gratitude for the student. This is a reflection, not part of the commentaries.

reflect.beginner: Is there something you understood only when someone showed you, after failing to work it out alone?
reflect.deeper: What does it mean that the god of death wishes for more students like this boy?
reflect.practice: Ask one real question this week of someone who knows more than you, and listen without arguing.

flags.note: āpaneyā: Śaṅkara glosses both ‘to be attained’ and ‘to be removed’; the derivation is not settled by the commentaries.
GRETIL’s प्रेष्टा for praṣṭā is classed as a witness error (corrections.json).
